entry.partOfSpeech: nouns and verbs (Priestly and Ezekielian cultic terminology); millēʾ yāḏ is a verbal idiom
entry.literal: sin, sin-offering / guilt, reparation / gift, tribute / well-being (offering) / slaughter, sacrifice / what is brought near / what is lifted off, contribution / toss, throw / cover, wipe clean / de-sin, purge / make clean / fill the hand
entry.standardEnglish: ASV: sin-offering / trespass-offering / meal-offering / peace-offerings / sacrifice / oblation / oblation (Ezekiel; 'heave-offering' in the Torah) / sprinkle / make atonement / cleanse / purify / consecrate. NRSV: sin offering / guilt offering / grain offering / offerings of well-being / sacrifice / offering / offering / dash / make atonement / purify / purify / consecrate (ordain). Milgrom (Leviticus, AB 3): purification offering / reparation offering
entry.wohChoice: ḥaṭṭāʾṯ 'sin-offering'; ʾāšām as a cultic noun 'guilt-offering'; minḥâ in a list of cultic offerings 'meal-offering' (the generic 'offering, gift, tribute' sense stays under minchah-shaah and minchah-tribute-gift-of-appeasement); šəlāmîm 'peace-offerings'; zeḇaḥ 'sacrifice'; qorbān 'offering'; tərûmâ 'oblation' (the Ezekiel usage, including the land allotment of Ezek 45 and 48; the Torah's tərûmâ to be reviewed when Leviticus and Numbers are translated); zāraq dām 'dash blood'; kippēr 'make atonement'; ḥiṭṭēʾ 'cleanse'; ṭihar 'purify'; millēʾ yāḏ 'consecrate', with the literal 'fill the hand' given in commentary. Compound offering names are hyphenated, as in olah-burnt-offering ('burnt-offering').
entry.rationale: The sacrificial terms of the Priestly code recur in Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Kings, Ezekiel and the Prophets. Ezek 40-46 uses almost the whole set in lists (40:39; 42:13; 44:29), so one decision should govern the corpus. The baseline is the ASV, whose terms the corpus already uses: 'burnt-offering' (central olah-burnt-offering), 'peace-offerings' (Ex 20:21 MT = 20:24 ET; 1 Kgs 8:63-64) and 'meal-offering' (1 Kgs 8:64). // Two ASV renderings are replaced by those of current versions. (1) For the cultic noun ʾāšām, 'guilt-offering' (NRSV, NJPS) replaces 'trespass-offering'; isaiah-woh already has 'guilt-offering' at Isa 53:10 under central ashem-asham-guilt-bearing-vocabulary, whose rationale names the sacrificial sense. (2) zāraq is to throw or dash liquid from a basin (mizrāq) against the altar (Ex 29:16, 20; Lev 1:5, 11). Sprinkling is a different act, hizzâ with the finger (Lev 4:6, 17; 16:14), and the Priestly ritual keeps the two apart (Milgrom, Leviticus 1-16, AB 3, 1991). The ASV 'sprinkle' for zāraq erases that distinction, so 'dash' (NRSV, NJPS) is used. // Milgrom's 'purification offering' for ḥaṭṭāʾṯ and 'reparation offering' for ʾāšām are widely discussed and recorded in commentary, but they are not adopted. The traditional terms are used by most versions, and 'sin-offering' keeps the link to the root ḥṭʾ 'sin', from which ḥaṭṭāʾṯ and the verb ḥiṭṭēʾ 'cleanse (from sin)' are formed. qorbān ('what is brought near', from qrb) is rendered 'offering' and tərûmâ ('what is lifted off', from rwm) keeps 'oblation', so that the ASV's single word 'oblation' no longer covers two lexemes. millēʾ yāḏ 'fill the hand' is the installation idiom (Ex 28:41; 29:9; Judg 17:5, 12), applied to the altar at Ezek 43:26 and rendered by its sense, 'consecrate', as in the ASV. // The decisions are lexical. The Raëlian canon's reading of the priestly dues of Ezek 44 as provisions for the creators (The Book Which Tells the Truth, ch. 3) is confined to labelled reception notes. // **Central housing.** The cluster is cross-corpus (Torah, Kings, Prophets, Psalms). The claim_type is direct because each rendering is either the ASV's or that of the main current versions.

changes.wohChoice: land. Context clause (ezekiel-woh wave E2): 'ground' where ʾereṣ is the ground level of a structure from which a height is measured (Ezek 42:6 mēhāʾāreṣ 'from the ground'; 43:14 mēḥêq hāʾāreṣ 'from the bottom on the ground').
changes.rationale:
אֶרֶץ in Hebrew covers a spectrum from 'patch of ground' to 'inhabited territory' to 'the whole inhabited world'. The capital-E 'Earth' (the planet) is a 17th-century-onwards English meaning that has no clean Hebrew equivalent. In Gen 1, אֶרֶץ is paired with שָׁמַיִם — they're a hendiadys for 'the whole physical setting'. 'Land' preserves the Hebrew register; 'earth' (lowercase, when the meaning is the dry ground as opposed to seas) is acceptable in some verses, but the default WoH choice is 'land'. Where the verse explicitly contrasts 'land' (dry) with 'seas' (water) (e.g. v10), 'land' is the more accurate choice anyway.

**Cross-corpus back-reference (Flood Story Editor pass, 2026-06).** The Hebrew *eretz* / *ha-aretz* is in cross-corpus cluster with the Sumerian *kalam* / *ka-na-aĝ2* — see the existing central entry `kalam-ka-na-ag-the-land-cross-corpus` (established at the Enki and Ninmaḫ Editor pass).

**Architectural context clause (ezekiel-woh wave E2, 2026-11).** In Ezekiel's measurements ʾereṣ twice denotes the ground level of a building or altar from which heights are reckoned (42:6, of the stories of the priests' chambers; 43:14, of the base of the altar). Neither 'land' nor 'earth' gives the sense, and the ASV, NRSV and NJPS all have 'ground'. The clause is lexical (BDB s.v. ʾereṣ, 'ground, surface of the ground') and does not change the default 'land', which governs the other Ezekiel sites of this wave (8:3, 12, 17; 11:15; 40:2; 43:2).

changes.rationale: 1 Kings 6-7 describes the Temple as a 'house' (*bayiṯ*) of three successive rooms on one axis: the *ʾûlām* in front (6:3), the *hêḵāl*, forty cubits long (6:17), and the *dəḇîr* at the rear, a twenty-cubit cube also called *qōḏeš haqqŏḏāšîm* and 'the inner house' (6:16, 19-20, 27). The same plan recurs in 2 Chr 3-4 and in Ezekiel's temple (Ezek 40:48-41:4), and it has close Iron Age parallels in north Syria (ʿAin Dara, Tell Tayinat; Monson, *BAR* 26/3, 2000; King and Stager, *Life in Biblical Israel*, 2001). // (1) *hêḵāl* is a loanword from Sumerian é.gal 'great house' via Akkadian *ekallu*, meaning 'palace' or 'temple' in general; in the plan it is the main room (HALOT *hêḵāl* 3). The ASV 'temple' is accurate for the general sense but misleading in 1 Kgs 6, where the whole building is the 'house' and 'the temple of the house' (6:3) names one of its rooms; 'great hall' (NJPS) keeps both the function of the room and the etymology. (2) *dəḇîr* is the rear room (HALOT 'back room'; cf. Arabic *dubr* 'back'). The ASV/KJV 'oracle' comes through the Vulgate *oraculum* from the ancient derivation of the word from *dbr* 'speak' (Aquila and Symmachus *chrēmatistērion*), which the modern lexica reject; the line uses 'inner sanctuary' (NRSV). (3) *ʾûlām* 'porch' and *qōḏeš haqqŏḏāšîm* 'the most holy place' (superlative construct, GKC §133i) are kept from the ASV. // The decision is lexical and architectural and carries no interpretive content. The Raëlian canon's description of the Temple as a residence built to receive the creators (*The Book Which Tells the Truth*, ch. 3) is recorded only in labelled reception notes in the chapter commentary. // **Central housing.** The terms recur in Kings, Chronicles, Ezekiel and the Psalms (*dəḇîr* Ps 28:2; *hêḵāl* passim), so one decision should govern the corpus; the claim_type is *direct* because the room functions and the lexical senses are uncontested in current scholarship. // **Ezekiel application (ezekiel-woh wave E2, 2026-11).** In Ezekiel's temple vision ʾûlām is 'porch' for the porch of each gate (ʾûlām haššaʿar, 40:7-9, 15, 39-40; 44:3) and for the porch of the Temple building (ʾûlām habbayiṯ, 40:48-49). The spelling ʾêlām (40:16-36), which the lexica treat as a by-form of ʾûlām, is rendered 'vestibule' under the ezekiel-woh overlay entry elam-vestibule-gate-element-ezekiel-40, so that the different spelling stays visible. hêḵāl is 'temple' under this entry's context clause where it names the building as a whole: at 8:16 the sun-worshippers stand in the court between the porch and the altar with 'their backs toward the hêḵāl' (so also NRSV and NJPS), and at 42:8 the hêḵāl is faced by the hundred-cubit side of the chamber block, matching the hundred-cubit length of the whole Temple (41:13). Where Ezek 41:1-4 measures the room between the porch and the inner sanctuary, the room is 'great hall' (later wave). habbayiṯ happənîmî 'the inner house' at 42:15 is rendered literally as listed above, but there it names the inner temple complex, not the dəḇîr as in 1 Kgs 6:27.
